Stock exposure. Settled in USDG.

A live pool-versus-trader system on Robinhood Chain: your wallet signs, contracts settle, and a shared vault backs the markets.

Updated 24 September 2026 · Live beta

{01}

Go long or short.

Choose a listed market to take synthetic exposure to its price in USDG. Long positions benefit from rising prices; shorts benefit from falling prices. Positions are leveraged and can lose their margin. You do not buy or own the underlying stock. This version uses a shared vault as the counterparty, not an order book or matching between traders.

{02}

How a trade reaches the chain.

Connect a wallet on Robinhood Chain and hold USDG for margin plus ETH for gas. Approve USDG when needed, deposit margin, then confirm the trade. The quote service checks market data and on-chain state, signs a short-lived quote, and prepares transaction data. Your wallet signs the transaction, and the clearing-house contract checks it before opening or closing exposure.

{03}

Where prices come from.

Goldlake uses a 5-minute time-weighted average from configured Uniswap v3 stock/USDG pools. An authorized signer attests to observations, and a publisher sends updates to the oracle contract. Freshness, confidence, and execution-deviation checks can block trades. This is not a direct stock-exchange feed or a multi-source TEE oracle. Charts aggregate stored observations into candles and refresh every 30 seconds while the page is visible.

{04}

Margin, limits, and liquidation.

Margin is tracked per wallet and market. Configured leverage, position limits, open-interest caps, and vault reserves limit how much exposure can be opened. Full liquidation is allowed when equity falls below maintenance requirements, subject to valid oracle data. A chart liquidation estimate helps show risk but does not promise a fill or payout at that price.

{05}

One vault backs the markets.

LPs deposit USDG and receive proportional vault shares. Settled trader losses can grow vault assets; trader profits reduce them. LP returns depend on those results, not a fixed APY. Vault withdrawals are wallet-signed and limited by available liquidity after reserves. Depositing USDG in the vault is different from depositing margin for your own trade.

{06}

Fees and the current version.

The quote service currently charges 0.06% of traded notional, with separate spreads and network gas. Fees go to the configured fee recipient, not an automatic LP reward. There are no periodic funding-rate payments in this version. Do not assume an order book, insurance tranche, staking yield, or permissionless market-listing system is available. The dashboard shows the markets currently configured.

{07}

Trust and beta status.

The contracts enforce settlement and risk checks, but quote issuance and oracle publication depend on running services and authorized keys. An administrative EOA controls important settings and signer permissions; the system is not fully trustless. Real funds are at risk during the beta. Read the risk disclosure, terms, and privacy information before using it.
